|strategy=By [mailto:zube@eagle.cc.ukans.edu Nick Zube]<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/astepbackward.html</ref>

This handy little Interrupt is great for both Podracer decks and your traditional Mains & Toys deck. And, with a great destiny of 5, it shouldn't be hard to fit in either deck type.

For its first function, [[A Step Backward]] takes both Podracers a step... well... backward. Placing all Podracers' top race destinies into their owners' Used Piles may seem like a lose-lose situation, but race destinies are like flame-broiled walruses: just one can do you in. If [[Sebulba]]'s just drawn a seven (modified to a ten!) and Anakin's stuck with a three or a four, who's going to suffer the most from [[A Step Backward]]? You can also use multiple copies of this handy card to prolong a race... a nice way to take maximum advantage of an opponent's "damaged" Podracer, wouldn't you say?

[[A Step Backward]]'s second function is risky, but sometimes, the biggest risks have the best payoffs. Discard [[A Step Backward]] and three random cards from your hand, and in exchange, you get to retrieve any character from your Lost Pile &#150; into your hand! It's like Premiere's "Back" cards on steroids! Use it as a last resort to save vital characters, like [[Han Solo]] for Profit decks, or even utilty characters, like [[Caldera Righim]].

[[A Step Backward]]? If it was up to me, I'd call this one a step forward!

A long race plus a "damaged" podracer equals bad news for [[Sebulba]].

Since Qui-Gon doesn't have a "back" card, use [[A Step Backward]] to return him to action if your [[Bacta Tank]]'s full.
